review_scope: Additional pure Topic-ownership handoff anchors; repository-internal structure, not engineering fact claims

reviews.basis: This anchor assigns gas sizing inputs and selected-travel ownership to the repository's gas-sizing Topic 7. The target pack contains explicit anchors for xT/xTP, expansion factor, gas coefficient and travel iteration. This confirms internal topic ownership only; it does not independently verify the underlying gas-sizing facts.

The source anchor assigns quantitative actuator/fail-safe sizing ownership. The target Pack contains actuator sizing and fail-action force-balance requirements; this confirms repository topic ownership, not an engineering calculation.
The source anchor is solely an ownership assignment for body/cage/guide and actuator-type selection. The target Pack explicitly owns guided-body forms and body/actuator selection.
The source anchor is solely an ownership assignment for seat leakage class, packing and fugitive emissions. The target Pack contains explicit anchors for all three subjects.

The source anchor assigns hardfacing, erosion-resistant material and severe-service construction as subjects to Topic 14; the target Pack contains explicit trim-material and severe-service construction anchors. This confirms repository ownership only, not material performance or selection suitability.

This anchor only assigns the internal repository ownership of cavitation, flashing, liquid choked-flow and FL-factor content to Topic 8. The target Pack contains explicit anchors for each named subject. It is a structural cross-reference, not independent proof of the physical statements in those target anchors.

This anchor assigns software development lifecycle and development V&V ownership to SW-04. The target Pack contains requirements, architecture, development change-impact, verification, validation and regression-test anchors. This confirms repository-internal subject ownership only, not the technical correctness of the target engineering claims.

This anchor assigns threat/compromise response and security-focused recovery ownership to SW-09, while SW-06 covers general approved-configuration and change recovery. The target Pack contains incident-response, trusted-recovery and security-backup anchors. This confirms repository ownership and handoff only; it does not establish a universal standard partition.

This anchor partitions operator-information/alarm ownership to SW-03 and underlying sequence/interlock state-transition ownership to SW-02. Both source and target Packs contain matching scope anchors. The review confirms internal ownership only, not universal standard terminology.

The boundary assigns SIL allocation, safety lifecycle, systematic-failure controls and Safety V&V content to the repository's SW-05, leaving SW-02 with operational logic/state-transition scope. Target Pack anchors cover those SW-05 subjects. This is repository taxonomy, not an external claim that standards use these SW numbers.

The anchor separates development lifecycle/V-Model/RTM ownership (SW-04) from project deliverables and site acceptance execution (SW-10). The named topics contain corresponding anchors; this confirms only the repository's intended allocation.
The anchor assigns interlock/trip state logic ownership to SW-02 and project records/test evidence to SW-10. Both Packs contain the assigned subjects. This is a structural cross-reference only.

The anchor assigns alarm/operator-information principles to SW-03 and approved project lists plus test/acceptance records to SW-10. The source and target Packs contain the related subjects; no external ownership rule is asserted.

The anchor assigns safety-integrity, systematic-failure and safety V&V scope to the repository's SW-05. Its target Pack contains matching lifecycle and verification subjects; this verifies internal scope ownership, not an external SW-number convention.

The anchor assigns detailed structural-coverage design and MC/DC code disposition to the dedicated coverage Pack, while SW-04 retains general software lifecycle and test scope. Both Packs explicitly cover these allocated subjects. The review does not reverify MC/DC technical requirements.
This reverse cross-reference assigns underlying interlock/trip logic to SW-02 and operator information/management to SW-03. Both Packs contain those scopes; it is an internal ownership boundary only.

The anchor assigns general software lifecycle/RTM/testing to SW-04 and project delivery/FAT/SAT/site execution to SW-10. The SW-04 and SW-10 Packs contain the declared topics; this is repository taxonomy, not a universal external allocation.

The anchor assigns protocol/medium/interoperability to SW-07 and measurable timing/synchronization/recovery attributes to SW-08. Target Pack scope anchors cover the assigned subject groups. The allocation is repository-internal.

This reverse cross-reference assigns quantitative network timing and recovery performance to SW-08 while SW-07 owns communication structure/interoperability. Both Packs contain the corresponding topics; no external standard numbering is asserted.

The anchor assigns cybersecurity controls and incident response to SW-09 while SW-07 owns communication function/selection. The target Pack contains the named security domains; this is a structural responsibility boundary only.

The anchor assigns detailed MC/DC pair, coverage-gap and code-disposition material to the dedicated MC/DC Pack while SW-05 retains the safety lifecycle context. Target Packs contain the declared subjects; this checks repository ownership only, not the underlying technical requirements.

The anchor allocates mechanical force/friction sizing, dynamic deadband/stiction testing, and conventional positioner/I/P principles across repository Topics 1, 3 and 11. The declared target Packs contain those scopes. This row records the primary Topic 1 linkage; see sibling topic owners in the source statement. Structural ownership only.

The anchor allocates seat leakage/packing, SIS/ESD/PST and full valve-package lifecycle to repository Topics 13, 15 and 16. The named target Packs contain matching subjects. This row records the Topic 13 linkage; the ownership statement is internal taxonomy, not a technical claim.

This anchor assigns smart-positioner diagnostics, valve signature and predictive maintenance to Topic 12. The target Pack contains diagnostics and signature evidence anchors; this verifies repository topic ownership only.

This anchor assigns SIS/ESD/PST and related safety-validation subjects to Topic 15. The target Pack contains final-element and partial-stroke-test scope anchors. This confirms internal subject ownership only.

This anchor assigns full valve-package datasheet, vendor-bid, installation and lifecycle workflow to Topic 16. The target Pack contains package selection ownership and specialist handoffs; this is repository structure, not a technical fact.

This anchor partitions actuator sizing, packing/dynamic behavior, and balanced/unbalanced trim subjects among repository Topics 1, 3 and 10. The selected target Packs contain the corresponding owners; the row confirms internal allocation only.

This anchor allocates positioner calibration, signature diagnostics and severe-service material/package design to repository Topics 11, 12 and 14. The report checks at least one matching anchor in every target Pack; it is an internal taxonomy cross-reference, not independent technical evidence.

The anchor assigns P&ID symbol/tag/loop/control-narrative design ownership to the P&ID Topic, while field installation implements approved documents. Its destination Pack contains diagram-scope, instrument-tag and loop-chain anchors. This is an internal document/installation boundary.

The anchor assigns hazardous-area classification and Ex/IS equipment selection to the hazardous-area Topic, while installation preserves the approved installation conditions. The destination Pack contains classification, selection and IS-system anchors; this confirms internal ownership only.

The anchor assigns power-system/grounding/shield design philosophy to the grounding Topic and limits the installation Topic to physical construction against approved drawings. The target Pack contains scope and PE/signal-reference anchors. This is repository topic ownership, not a grounding prescription.

The anchor assigns field installation construction/inspection ownership to the installation Topic and leaves qualification to assess representative installed conditions. Destination Pack anchors cover the assigned installation subjects; this confirms internal topic partition only.

The anchor assigns overall hardware architecture/component-selection lifecycle to the hardware Topic and specifies environment/EMC qualification as this Topic's subdomain. The target Pack contains architecture, selection and verification scope anchors. This is repository ownership only.

The anchor assigns component-level electronic error chains to the electronics-error Topic and environment qualification outcomes to this Topic. The destination Pack contains error-chain anchors; this review verifies only the repository's scope assignment.

This anchor assigns fieldbus/Ethernet/wireless protocol and gateway selection details to the communications Topic while this Topic owns higher-layer Device–Edge–Platform integration. Destination anchors match the allocated subject; internal routing only.

This anchor assigns historian/MES/ERP time-series, data-quality, retention/governance and genealogy detail to the historian/MES Topic, while the IIoT Topic consumes those data functions at the platform layer. Destination anchors cover the assigned subjects; this is a repository ownership cross-reference.

The anchor assigns selection of governing codes/editions/specifications and deviation approval to the design-basis Topic, while the installation Topic implements approved criteria in the field. The destination Pack contains governing-document and deviation-governance anchors. This confirms internal responsibility allocation only.

This anchor assigns FAT/SAT, loop-test, commissioning, performance-test, acceptance and handover execution to SW-10. The target Pack contains project execution, FAT, SAT and acceptance anchors; this validates internal topic ownership only.

This anchor declares repository ownership for non-explosion environmental safe-state/fail-safe topics and assigns detailed Ex/IS, environmental qualification, grounding/UPS and SIL/SIS lifecycle subjects to their respective Packs. Matching target scope anchors are present. This confirms content routing only and does not validate the safe-state or fail-safe technical claims themselves.

This anchor only assigns booster bypass/sensitivity dynamic-tuning ownership to the repository's Topic 3. The target pack explicitly owns booster-flow/feedback conditions, hunting diagnosis and positioner gain/stability tradeoffs. This confirms repository topic ownership only, not an engineering tuning prescription.

The source anchor assigns plant/panel grounding, shield-termination and field EMC ownership to the grounding/EMC Topic and retains PCB-local electronic error contributors in its own Topic. The target Pack contains explicit grounding, shield and diagnostic anchors. This confirms repository routing only; it does not independently verify the technical content of either Topic.

The source anchor allocates environmental/EMC qualification setup, stress, monitoring and qualification evidence to the environmental qualification Topic while retaining electronic error mechanisms in the source Topic. The target Pack contains scope, requirement-traceability and report-evidence anchors. This is an internal scope handoff only.

The source anchor allocates hardware architecture, component-selection governance and design/production verification lifecycle ownership to the hardware lifecycle Topic. The destination Pack contains anchors for lifecycle scope, component selection, design verification and production-test coverage. This confirms internal ownership only.

The source anchor assigns final-element SIS/ESD integrity, PST and proof-test credit to the dedicated final-element safety Topic, and control-valve package selection and lifecycle economics to the dedicated valve selection/lifecycle Topic. The cited destination anchors exist. This confirms repository topic ownership only and does not validate any technical claim in those destination anchors.

The source anchor assigns each named sensor family's sensing principle and sensor-specific compensation ownership to its corresponding sensor Topic, while this Topic covers shared electronics error contributors. The listed destination anchors exist across the RTD, thermocouple, strain/load-cell, LVDT/RVDT and piezoelectric Packs. This confirms repository topic allocation only, not the technical truth of those sensor anchors.

The source assigns authentication, encryption, access control, firewall, and cyber-incident response to the repository's SW-09 pack; the target contains matching anchors. This confirms repository-internal topic ownership only, not engineering or cybersecurity correctness.

The source assigns alarm/HMI operator-response ownership to the dedicated HMI/SCADA pack; the target has matching alarm and operator-authority anchors. This is repository topic ownership only, not external proof of the safety or alarm claims.

scope_reviews.basis: The anchor defines the repository's SW-02 subject coverage and groups sequence, state-transition, protection and recovery mechanisms under one operational-logic topic; it is not an external technical assertion. The same Pack contains the named subject anchors. This confirms internal scope consistency only, not the truth of the technical claims in those anchors.

This Anchor defines Topic 16 ownership and its integration relationship to adjacent specialist Packs. It is an internal topic-boundary statement, not an external engineering fact; the downstream technical Anchors require independent evidence review.

This Anchor names the Pack's subject and links smart-positioner diagnostic signals, signature testing and maintenance use. It is an internal scope declaration; each technical diagnostic claim still requires independent evidence.

This anchor explicitly limits Topic 15 to the final-element subsystem contribution and defers general SIS/SIF/SIL allocation theory. It is an internal ownership boundary, not an independently verified technical proposition.

This anchor declares the repository's project-execution subject boundary for SW-10. It is an internal taxonomy statement; the technical content of each project activity remains independently reviewable.
This Anchor describes the repository's subject scope and internal lifecycle flow for the hardware Pack. It is a scope statement, not a verified universal hardware lifecycle standard.
This Anchor hands detailed noise/drift/aging error propagation to the dedicated EEM Pack; this is an internal topic ownership boundary only.
This Anchor assigns grounding/shield/EMC principles to the dedicated power-grounding Pack and limits the hardware Pack to applying their requirements; this is repository-internal scope.
This Anchor assigns site cable/wiring/tubing installation and inspection to the installation Pack and panel-internal production wiring to the hardware Pack; the split is repository taxonomy.
This Anchor assigns detailed environmental and EMC test setup/acceptance ownership to the environmental qualification Pack; it does not assert an external universal standard partition.
This Anchor distinguishes product hardware design/production evidence from project-level FAT/SAT/commissioning ownership. It is an internal cross-topic allocation.
This Anchor assigns software lifecycle/verification ownership to the SW-04 Pack and hardware lifecycle evidence to the present Pack; this is a repository-local boundary.
This Anchor describes the repository scope of installation quality as an end-to-end chain. It is an internal topic summary, not a universal installation standard definition.
This Anchor assigns shield termination design decisions to the grounding/EMC Pack and limits the installation Pack to implementing approved drawings; this is repository-local ownership.

This Anchor allocates overall project FAT/SAT/commissioning acceptance to the project Pack while assigning site installation evidence here; it is a cross-Pack boundary, not an external standards statement.

This Anchor declares the repository's own SW-04 coverage from requirements through verification evidence. The referenced anchors exist in the same Pack; this is an internal scope statement, not an independently verified lifecycle requirement or safety standard claim.

This Anchor declares the repository's SW-03 scope for operator information and alarm/event management and references subjects present in the same Pack. It is an internal Topic boundary, not a claim that one external standard mandates this exact Pack organization.

unresolved_scope_reviews.basis: The anchor assigns general accuracy, precision, repeatability, uncertainty and calibration-traceability definitions to a generic metrology/calibration owner, but the current Topic Pack inventory has no clearly named general metrology Topic covering that full set. The calibration-operations Topic covers traceability and interval management, not every listed general definition. Do not classify this as a verified ownership boundary until a concrete owner and matching anchors are identified.
